result.summary: REGATE PASS. Verified `git diff main...HEAD -- lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex` matches design doc iss0699-test-parallel-tmpdir-cleanup-fix.md §3a exactly: (1) stream_and_capture/2 -> /3 with `env \\ []` default, threaded into Port.open's :env opts list, converted name/value to charlists only when non-empty -- correct per OTP's :env port option requiring charlists/atoms not binaries, and the three other call sites (run_discovery_dry_run/0, run_single_wasm_hang_test/1, run_lua_wallclock_race_tests/0) stay 2-arity/unaffected (confirmed not in the diff). (2) run_main_suite/0's one call site (line ~173) now passes [{"TEST_PARALLEL_KEEP_LOGS", "1"}], scoped to only that invocation, matching §3a.2. (3) the {:ok, log_dir} branch binds native_log_dir and wraps check_main_suite_logs/2 in try/after with File.rm_rf!(native_log_dir) in the after clause -- covers all four of that function's outcomes (zero logs, real failures/report_partition_failures, ISS-0069 substring match, clean :ok pass) since Elixir's after fires on both normal return and Mix.raise's raised exception; read-before-delete ordering holds by try/after evaluation order, not timing. ISS-0069 substring-check logic (@target_substring, find_partition_log_dir/1, check_substring_across_logs/1, report_partition_failures/1) does not appear anywhere in the diff -- provably untouched. No scope creep: diff is confined to stream_and_capture/2->3 and the one run_main_suite/0 call site/branch; scripts/test_parallel.sh's diff (trap/cleanup function) matches design §2, unchanged from the already-PASSed iteration-0 review (prior PASS on that file stands). No contradiction with docs/migration/decisions/0009-test-parallel-pool-sizing.md (pool-sizing arithmetic untouched) or lib/letflow/design/iss0428-parallel-runner-in-check-test.md (log-dir discovery/shell-out contract unchanged; this change only moves temp-dir lifetime ownership from the script's trap to the caller, which composes with, not contradicts, ISS-0428's design). No OTP idiom/supervision concerns -- this is Mix-task/tooling code, no process/supervision surface involved.
